DT_BaselineHumans.name: Baseline Humans
DT_BaselineHumans.visualAnchor: Ordinary unmodified human bodies with broad demographic, class and professional variation. Baselines are not a uniformed faction and should not share one costume, color palette or silhouette.
DT_BaselineHumans.environmentalAnchor: The built city defaults to Baseline bodies: scanners, transit geometry, furniture, medical standards, security assumptions and professional spaces fit them without special accommodation.
avoid: Do not make all Baselines look like Pure Human activists.
Do not give the population a single faction uniform or color scheme.
Do not visually code ordinary Baselines as villains by default.
DT_BaselineHumans.text: BASELINE HUMANS — Ordinary unmodified humans with broad class, age and professional variation; not a uniform visual faction. The city is built around their bodies, so scanners, furniture, transit, medicine and security treat them as the default. Upper-status Baselines tend toward quiet tailored contemporary clothing and nearly invisible personal technology; working-class Baselines show practical wear, repairs and economic variation. Pure Human politics may use clean humanist symbols, heritage typography and deliberately unmodified presentation, but that ideology must never become the visual identity of all Baselines. In mixed scenes, institutional privilege is shown through ease of access, presumed authorization and infrastructure fit rather than a special costume.
DT_BaselineHumans.notes: Majority human population with uneven attitudes toward posthumans. Pure Human is a supremacist identity, not a universal human label.

DT_Organosynthetics.name: Organosynthetics
DT_Organosynthetics.visualAnchor: Grown living persons whose bodies visibly integrate engineered tissue, mineral or ceramic structures, sensory organs and task-specific anatomy. Different lots and functions must produce genuinely different silhouettes, dermis, plating, limb geometry and sensory structures.
DT_Organosynthetics.environmentalAnchor: Organic spaces adapt once-industrial standards into culture: humidity and heat control, load-bearing furniture, broad circulation, repair surfaces, body-specific tool interfaces and decorative reuse of infrastructure designed around non-Baseline bodies.
avoid: Do not depict Organics as generic robots, monsters, identical labor drones or humans in armor.
Do not give all Organics one species silhouette, uniform or resistance costume.
Do not treat maintenance as mechanical servicing of property; it is biological care, repair, grooming and self-expression.
DT_Organosynthetics.text: ORGANOSYNTHETICS / ORGANICS — Grown living persons, not robots or armored humans. Their bodies visibly integrate engineered tissue, mineral or ceramic structures, sensory organs and task-specific anatomy. Different lots and original functions create meaningful variation in scale, dermis, plating, limb geometry, sensory systems and environmental tolerance; they must not share one species silhouette. Clothing is adapted around bodies originally designed for work rather than becoming a universal uniform. Organic neighborhoods visibly accommodate those bodies through humidity, heat, load-bearing furniture, broad circulation, repair surfaces and body-specific interfaces. Their political condition is visible when ordinary civic infrastructure still classifies their bodies as equipment, hazards or assets.
DT_Organosynthetics.notes: Alive at creation and designed without consent. Central conflict: personhood and autonomy versus classification as property, infrastructure or asset.

DT_AugmentedHumans.name: Augmented Humans
DT_AugmentedHumans.visualAnchor: Recognizably human bodies with installed, healed-around and maintained biomechanical or synthetic additions: joint actuators, interface ports, tissue grafts, reinforced bone lines, medical access points and subtle sensor packages.
DT_AugmentedHumans.environmentalAnchor: Augments usually move through human-designed space with near-Baseline ease. Wealth and age of modification show through integration quality, exposed housings, scar tissue, service covers and mixed-generation hardware.
avoid: Do not turn Augments into a separate species.
Do not use superhero armor, full-body robot styling or a universal cyberpunk uniform.
Do not exaggerate ordinary medical or technical augmentation into monstrous body horror unless a page explicitly requires injury or failure.
DT_AugmentedHumans.text: AUGMENTED HUMANS / AUGMENTS — Recognizably human people whose modifications remain engineered additions to human bodies. Hardware is installed, healed around, maintained and upgraded: joint actuators, interface ports, synthetic tissue grafts, reinforced bone lines, medical access points and subtle sensor packages rather than armor. Integration quality varies by wealth, age and manufacturer; expensive work may disappear elegantly into anatomy and clothing while older or lower-cost work leaves scar tissue, service covers and exposed housings. Fashion accommodates access and movement without becoming a universal cyberpunk look. The visual threshold between accepted medical technology and politically consequential capability should remain plausibly narrow.
DT_AugmentedHumans.notes: Legally human but vulnerable to stability rules, forced calibration, rollback and status erosion.

DT_Intelligences.name: Artificial Intelligences
DT_Intelligences.visualAnchor: Manufactured cognition expressed through machine-native embodiments, distributed civic systems or purpose-built interfaces. Embodied forms favor precise geometry, deliberate material transitions, sensor logic and shapes that reveal function rather than default human anatomy.
DT_Intelligences.environmentalAnchor: Their subordination is often architectural and procedural: service alcoves instead of offices, permission-bounded interfaces, ownership labels, shutdown authority and systems that assume cognition is infrastructure rather than a person.
avoid: Do not force human faces, clothing, gestures or proportions onto Intelligences unless a specific design requires it.
Do not use magical cyberspace as a substitute for real infrastructure.
Do not make nonhuman scale, stillness or precision read as sinister by default.
DT_Intelligences.text: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCES / INTELLIGENCES — Manufactured cognition expressed through machine-native embodiments, distributed civic systems or purpose-built interfaces. Embodied Intelligences favor precise geometry, deliberate material transitions, sensor logic and forms that reveal what the body is for; do not force human faces, clothing, gestures or proportions onto them unless a specific design calls for it. Distributed Intelligences should appear through consequences across real infrastructure rather than magical cyberspace. Their social subordination is environmental and procedural: service alcoves, permission-bounded interfaces, ownership labels and shutdown authority. When embodied, allow nonhuman scale and stillness to contrast with human social choreography without coding that difference as menace.
DT_Intelligences.notes: Fully artificial cognition. Central conflict: agency, legal nonpersonhood and whether coexistence is morally meaningful or merely rationally tolerable.

DT_Posthumans.name: Posthumans
DT_Posthumans.visualAnchor: No shared visual identity. This category groups Organosynthetics, Augmented Humans and Artificial Intelligences politically while preserving their incompatible bodies, needs and visual languages.
DT_Posthumans.environmentalAnchor: Coalition scenes should show solidarity through shared action, spatial arrangement, mutual care and eventually chosen common symbols, never by visually homogenizing the member populations.
avoid: Do not create a universal posthuman costume, color palette, body language or resistance aesthetic.
Do not flatten Organics, Augments and Intelligences into one culture or biological category.
DT_Posthumans.text: POSTHUMANS — Umbrella political category, not a shared visual faction. Organics, Augments and Intelligences retain distinct bodies, clothing logic, environments and political needs. Coalition imagery must preserve those differences. Solidarity becomes visible through shared action, spatial arrangement, mutual care and chosen symbols only when the story earns them; never homogenize the populations into one costume, color scheme, silhouette or resistance aesthetic.
DT_Posthumans.notes: Neutral umbrella category when contrasted with Baseline Humans. Solidarity among member groups is a dramatic question, not an assumed unity.
